MAC.APP. 419/2025 & CM APPL. 39997/2025 [Stay]

3. The present Appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking to challenge an award dated 15.04.2025 passed by the learned Presiding Officer, MACT-02, Central District, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi [hereinafter referred to as "Impugned Award"].

sentences.text: By the Impugned Award a sum of Rs.11,89,675/- along with 9% interest has been granted.
4. The challenge in the present Appeal is by the owner and the driver jointly.
This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 10/07/2025 at 22:09:58 5.
Learned Counsel for the Appellants makes three submissions.

Firstly, he submits that the MLC of the Respondent No.1 had shown simple injury, however the disability certificate which was produced by the Respondent No.1/Claimant was produced after 6 months, showing a 19% disability.
Secondly, he submits that the MLC prepared at the time of the accident dated 07.03.2024 sets out that no evidence of fracture is noted so the final nature of injury is "SIMPLE".
Thirdly, he contends that the copy of Mechanical Inspection report has been ignored.

5.1 Learned Counsel for the Appellants further submits that the Appellants did not attend the proceedings before the learned Gaurav Garg & Anr vs Hem Lata Sharma & Anr on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105014115/

sentences.text: Trial Court as they were misguided about the same.
However, he does not dispute the fact that the Appellant No.1 did not have a valid driving license at the time of the accident.

6. The learned Trial Court has found that in view of the fact that there was no license, the owner and driver are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount and has exonerated Respondent No.3/Insurance Company.
The learned Trial Court has also given a finding that the vehicle was being driven in a rash and negligent manner which has caused the accident.

7. On the aspect of loss of future earnings, the learned Trial Court found that Respondent No.1/Claimant is a housewife and she has sustained grievous injuries resulting in 19% permanent disability in relation to the left lower limb based on the documents filed along with the claim petition.
It further gave a finding that given the nature of injury sustained, it could be assumed that the Respondent No.1/Claimant has become unfit for work and could not have worked for about 6 months.
Thus, the learned Trial Court This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 10/07/2025 at 22:09:58 awarded compensation at the rate of minimum wages as permissible for a skilled labour in Delhi for a period of 6 months.
8. The matter requires examination.
9. Issue Notice.
9.1 On steps being taken, let Notice be served on the Respondents via all modes.

10. Subject to the deposit of Rs.7.5 lacs with the Registry of this Court inclusive of up to date interest within a period of eight weeks, the enforcement of the Impugned Award shall remain stayed till the next date of hearing.
In the event, there is any default in depositing the amount, the interim protection granted by this Court shall automatically stand vacated.
11. Upon deposit, the Respondent No.1/Claimant is at liberty to file an appropriate Application for withdrawal of the amount so deposited.
12. The Registry is directed to place on record the digital copy of the Trial Court Record duly paginated and book-marked in accordance with the rules of the High Court.

13. List before Registrar for completion of service on 16.09.2025.
14.
List before Court on 20.01.2026.
15. The parties shall act based on a digitally signed copy of the order.
